summary: Settlement posting stalled at ~07:42Z because the order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 07:40Z) broke the OrderExecuted payload contract: the event renamed field qty->quantity, added venue, and added an event schema version header v2, while settlement-service's consumer still validates against schema v1. The consumer cannot deserialize offset orders-3@8841207 ('missing required field qty, schema v1 expected, header says v2'), treats it as a poison message, and blocks partition orders-3, so lag grows monotonically to ~60k with no settlements posted. Confidence in H1 is medium (0.60), clearly ahead of the alternatives, and it is supported by an exact verbatim match between dep-6010's declared change set and the first ERROR, by the ~2-minute deploy-to-failure timing, and by the absence of any rebalance/pool evidence that would support the suspected consumer poll-settings change (cfg-3004). Residual uncertainty is that no producer-side or schema-registry telemetry directly proves dep-6010 emitted the v2 message at that offset.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service dep-6010 emitted v2 OrderExecuted schema that settlement-service cannot deserialize, blocking a partition
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 07:40Z) changed the OrderExecuted event schema (renamed qty->quantity, added venue, added schema-version header v2) while settlement-service's consumer still validates against schema v1. The consumer fails to deserialize offset orders-3@8841207 ('missing required field qty'), treats it as a poison message, and blocks partition orders-3, so no further settlements are posted and lag grows monotonically. The fault originates in the order-service producer contract break.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6010 deployed to order-service at 07:40Z changes OrderExecuted schema: qty->quantity, add venue, header v2
order-service begins producing v2 OrderExecuted messages onto topic 'orders' (partition orders-3)
settlement-service consumer validates against v1, cannot deserialize the v2 record at offset 8841207 ('missing required field qty, schema v1 expected, header says v2')
the un-deserializable record becomes a poison message retried indefinitely on orders-3, blocking the partition
partition blocked -> consumer commits nothing -> lag grows monotonically (603 at 07:42 to ~60k at 09:55) and zero settlements post

assumptions: The v2 messages on orders-3 were produced by order-service and not by a different producer (F3 change set matches, but no producer-side telemetry confirms the specific record)
settlement-service has no forward-compatible/v2 schema handling
The 'zero settlements processed' symptom follows from the blocked partition (no direct settlement counter metric)

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service consumer.max.poll.records change (cfg-3004) caused processing/rebalance failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The settlement-service config change cfg-3004 (07:35Z) reducing max.poll.records 500->200 caused the consumer to fail to process or to be rebalanced, so lag grows. This is the reporter's suspicion.

causal_chain.claim: the reduced batch size disrupts the consumer group / causes rebalance, stalling processing (assumed mechanism)
consumer stops committing, lag grows to ~60k, zero settlements

assumptions: A max.poll.records reduction can produce a rebalance or hard consumer failure — contradicted by the absence of any rebalance/pool event (F12)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Mechanism mismatch and no supporting signature: the only error is a schema/deserialization failure keyed to dep-6010's declared change (F8/F17), and logs show zero rebalance or pool events on settlement-service (F12). A batch-size reduction cannot itself cause a 'missing required field qty (header says v2)' error (F18). Timing is also looser (7 min vs 2 min gap).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka broker degradation / partition reassignment starves the consumer independent of any service change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Broker-side trouble (partition reassignment, rebalance storm, or produce-side starvation) stalls settlement-service's consumer independently of settlement-service config. Supported by two historical incidents citing kafka partition reassignment/rebalance.

causal_chain.claim: kafka broker undergoes partition reassignment / rebalance affecting orders-3 (assumed)
settlement consumer loses assignment or is starved, lag grows

assumptions: A broker event occurred without any recorded config/deploy change (F5 shows none)
The historical rebalance-pattern leads (F6) apply to this incident
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Zero rebalance events on settlement-service (F12) directly falsifies the rebalance mechanism; no kafka change recorded (F5/F19); the observed error is a deterministic poison-message block at a specific offset with a schema mismatch, not starvation; historical leads are match_score-only and contradict this incident's mechanism (F20).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Downstream backpressure (ledger-db) or resource saturation on settlement-service stalls processing
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Backpressure from ledger-db or CPU/DB-connection saturation on settlement-service stalls the consumer so messages are fetched but never committed. Lag grows without upstream involvement.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db write latency or settlement-service resource saturation slows processing
consumer falls behind and commits nothing, lag grows

assumptions: Some unmeasured backpressure exists despite flat db_pool_in_use
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: db_pool_in_use stayed flat ~5.85-6.17 and CPU elevated but not saturated (F11); no ledger-db change (F5/F19); the stall is explained by a specific deserialization/poison-message block (F8/F9), not throughput degradation.

facts.statement: Exactly two changes occurred across ALL services in 07:00Z-09:59Z on 2026-05-12: a settlement-service config change consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 at 07:35:00Z (author m.das) and the order-service deploy dep-6010 v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z; both preceded the 08:22Z report.

dep-6010 (order-service, v2.16.0, 07:40Z, status live, rolled_back_at null) changed the OrderExecuted event schema: field rename qty -> quantity, added field 'venue', and added an event schema version header v2; order-service is an upstream producer of the events settlement-service consumes.
Settlement consumer lag was at baseline through the 07:40Z bucket (avg 31.06) and jumped to avg 603.29 / max 819.95 in the 07:42:00Z bucket, placing onset between 07:40 and 07:42.

The first ERROR on settlement-service in the window is a deserialization failure at 07:42:14Z: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'; the pattern fired 213 times.

A second error pattern follows: 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked' (196 occurrences, first_seen 07:44:51Z) — the same offset on orders-3 is retried indefinitely, stalling the partition.

The deploy's declared change set matches the error signature verbatim: dep-6010 names 'rename field qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', 'event schema version header v2', and the first ERROR names exactly 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' at orders-3@8841207.
Timing favors the deploy over the poll change: dep-6010 at 07:40:00Z precedes the first failed offset by ~2 minutes, whereas cfg-3004 at 07:35:00Z precedes it by ~7 minutes.

Settlement lag grew monotonically and did not recover: 603 (07:42), 20,525 avg / 22,062 max (08:25:34), 60,220.76 avg / 61,605.53 max (09:55); all 409 matched log lines in 07:00-09:59 were ERROR level.
No rebalance or connection-pool log events were found on settlement-service in 07:00-09:59 ('rebalance' and 'pool' searches both returned total_matched 0).

No resource saturation or DB pool exhaustion on settlement-service: db_pool_in_use stayed flat ~5.85-6.17 avg (max 6.78) over 160 points 07:20-09:52; cpu_pct rose from ~28.68% avg to ~69-71% avg (max 78.28%) — elevated but not saturated.

order-service shows no error signal correlated with settlement onset: only 2 WARN lines in 07:00-09:59 (connection-reset retry 07:22:50Z, slow /internal/metrics 09:14:44Z), neither coinciding with the 07:42 onset.
settlement-service depends on kafka (queue-consume) and ledger-db (db); both are shared:true and owned by 'platform', and neither had any deploy or config change recorded on 2026-05-12.

The consumer poll-settings change cfg-3004 has no corresponding failure signature: no consumer-group rebalance or pool events on settlement-service, and a batch-size reduction cannot itself produce a schema/deserialization error, so its 07:35Z position is timing-only.

Historical leads do not match this incident's mechanism: HIST-112 and HIST-104 both cite kafka partition reassignment/rebalance, but zero rebalance events were found, and a search for deserialization/schema-mismatch precedents returned 0 incidents.

assumptions: The v2-header OrderExecuted records on partition orders-3 were produced by order-service dep-6010; the deploy's declared change set matches the error verbatim, but no producer-side telemetry or schema-registry record confirms the specific message at offset 8841207.
settlement-service has no forward-compatible / v2 schema handling, so a v2 payload is a hard deserialization failure for its consumer.
The 'zero settlements processed' symptom follows from the blocked partition; there is no directly measured processed-settlements counter among available metrics.
order-service is the only upstream producer of the OrderExecuted events consumed by settlement-service on topic 'orders'; a full producer enumeration for kafka could not be completed.

timeline.event: settlement-service config change cfg-3004: consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 by m.das ('Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes') — the reporter's suspected cause.
order-service deploy dep-6010 v2.16.0 goes live, changing the OrderExecuted event schema (qty->quantity, added venue, added schema-version header v2).
Last normal settlement lag bucket: avg 31.06.
First elevated lag bucket: avg 603.29 / max 819.95 — onset between 07:40 and 07:42.
First ERROR on settlement-service: deserialization failure at orders-3@8841207, 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'; 213 occurrences.
Second error pattern: 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked' (196 occurrences) — partition orders-3 blocked.
Incident INC-010 reported by on-call SRE: no settlements posted ~40 minutes, settlement consumer lag growing.
Resource check: db_pool_in_use flat ~5.85-6.17 (max 6.78) over 160 points; cpu_pct elevated ~69-71% avg (max 78.28%), not saturated.
Settlement lag ~60,220.76 avg / 61,605.53 max — approximately 60k and climbing, no recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0) to the last v1-schema-producing version so order-service resumes emitting OrderExecuted with field 'qty' and no v2 schema-version header, unblocking partition orders-3.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-6010's declared change set (qty->quantity, venue, v2 header) matches the settlement-service deserialization error verbatim at orders-3@8841207, and it deployed ~2 minutes before onset (F3, F7, F8, F16, F17). dep-6010 is still 'live' with rolled_back_at null (F3), so a rollback is available and is the fastest way to stop producing v2 payloads.

recommended_actions.action: After rollback, unblock/skip the poison offset on partition orders-3 (reset consumer offset past orders-3@8841207 or acked-skip the poison record) via settlement-service's consumer tooling.
recommended_actions.rationale: The consumer retries the same offset indefinitely ('poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 ... partition blocked', 196 occurrences), so the partition stays blocked even after the producer is fixed unless the stuck record is bypassed (F9, F14).

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT revert the settlement-service poll-settings change cfg-3004 as the primary mitigation, and do not treat it as the cause.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-3004 has no failure signature: zero rebalance/pool events on settlement-service, flat db_pool_in_use, and a batch-size reduction cannot produce a schema/deserialization error; its 07:35Z position is timing-only (F11, F12, F18).

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery: confirm settlement consumer lag returns to baseline (~26-55) and drains, the 'missing required field qty' and 'poison message ... partition blocked' error patterns stop, and CPU settles below the elevated ~69-71% plateau.
recommended_actions.rationale: Lag grew monotonically to ~60k with 409 ERROR lines and no recovery, so restoration must be demonstrated by lag drain plus cessation of both error patterns and CPU normalization (F8, F9, F10, F11).

recommended_actions.action: Add forward-compatible schema handling on settlement-service (accept/ignore unknown fields, tolerate a v2 schema-version header) and add a schema-compatibility gate so producer contract changes are caught before rollout.
recommended_actions.rationale: The consumer discarded the whole partition on a single unknown field, a hard failure mode for any future additive producer change; forward compatibility would have made qty->quantity plus an added field non-breaking (F8, F17).

recommended_actions.action: Adopt a producer/consumer contract-test or schema-registry compatibility check in the order-service and settlement-service release pipeline, and add a dead-letter-queue path so a poison message does not block an entire partition.
recommended_actions.rationale: The incident was caused by an unreviewed producer contract break (dep-6010) plus a consumer design that blocks the partition on one bad record; both need pipeline and consumer-level prevention to avoid recurrence (F3, F9, F17).

recommended_actions.action: Alert on poison-message / deserialization error rate and partition-blocked conditions (not only on lag), so a blocked partition pages immediately instead of being discovered via a downstream lag report.
recommended_actions.rationale: The two ERROR patterns fired at 07:42:14Z and 07:44:51Z but the incident was only reported at 08:22Z (~40 minutes later) — earlier detection of these signatures shortens exposure (F8, F9, F10).

data_gaps: Tool-call budget was exhausted before the final two parallel queries (get_service_dependencies for kafka and a second historical-incident search), so the full set of upstream producers feeding settlement-service's kafka topic beyond order-service is unconfirmed, and no precedent linking a producer schema change to consumer stalls was found.

get_config_changes/get_deployments were only queried per-service for kafka, order-service, and ledger-db plus one all-services call starting at 07:00Z; the window 00:00Z-07:00Z for other services was not fully enumerated, so a pre-07:00Z change by a third service affecting settlement-service could have been missed.

Broker/topic metrics (produce rate, partition lag distribution, bytes in/out) could not be queried and no kafka-broker available_metrics listing was obtained, so upstream starvation vs consumer-side stall cannot be separated from broker-side metrics.
kafka-broker and trade-service log searches were not executed, so no broker-side or alternate-consumer error signatures could be gathered.

No producer-side log, deploy telemetry, or schema-registry record was retrieved to identify the actor that began emitting v2 OrderExecuted events, so the identity of the schema-changing producer (inferred to be order-service dep-6010) is not independently confirmed.

No metric-based evidence of 'zero settlements processed' exists among available metrics (consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so that symptom is inferred from the blocked-partition lag shape rather than directly measured.

No producer-side or schema-registry telemetry confirms the specific record at offset orders-3@8841207 was produced by dep-6010; the link rests on the deploy's declared change set matching the error text exactly.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Producer-side or schema-registry evidence showing the v2-header OrderExecuted records on orders-3 were emitted by a service other than order-service (or by a producer unchanged by dep-6010).
Rolling back dep-6010 without any other change yet finding the partition still blocked and the 'missing required field qty' errors persisting, which would point away from the producer contract break.

Recovery of settlement lag with no rollback of dep-6010 (e.g. after only cfg-3004 reverted or a consumer restart), which would support the poll-settings change (H2) or a transient/broker cause instead.
Discovery of consumer-group rebalance, partition-reassignment, or pool-exhaustion events on settlement-service in a fuller log/metric query, which would revive H2 or H3.

Evidence of a broker-side event (partition reassignment, produce starvation) or a ledger-db change on 2026-05-12 that was outside the queried per-service windows, which would support an infrastructure cause (H3/H4).
A finding that settlement-service actually does have forward-compatible v2 handling, which would break the deserialization mechanism underlying H1.

findings.statement: Interpretation: the settlement stall is consumer-side and schema-driven — messages on topic 'orders' partition 3 are being produced with header schema v2 while the settlement consumer expects v1 ('header says v2'), so the consumer cannot deserialize offset 8841207 and blocks the whole partition. The growing lag is the blocked partition accumulating, not upstream produce failure. The reported 'consumer poll settings change' is not reflected in any rebalance/pool error in the logs.
